subject: GPU lane scenarios & staged on-ramp — Northforge Therapeutics
messages:
From: Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@northforge.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity options — initial context

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're evaluating a dedicated lane for inference of our clinical triage model (sequence length ~2k, peak concurrent reqs ~220). We need guidance on a) minimum set of GPUs to guarantee p95 latency <350ms for 2k tokens, b) sensible ramp schedule over the first 9 months, and c) how to structure a deal so we can scale without re-negotiating every quarter.

Can you share a few sensible sizing bundles and what the trade-offs are (cost vs buffer vs SLA)? Also please include any warm-up or pre-warm recommendations if we reserve a smaller floor initially.

Thanks,
Arjun Rao
Head of ML Platforms
Northforge Therapeutics

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@northforge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity options — initial context

Arjun — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a concise proposal with three lane profiles (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) and a month-by-month ramp. High level:

- Conservative: 32 A100s equiv min (floor) with burst to 48 — lowest operational risk, higher committed cost.
- Balanced: 20 A100s equiv min with automated burst to 36 — good middle ground for predictable growth.
- Aggressive (pilot-first): 8 A100s equiv min, with fast ramp triggers and warm-start credits — lowest commit, higher burst risk and potential SLA exceptions if bursts saturate.

Attached: Northforge_Onramp_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal) and a sizing workbook. Karthik, can you add the perf/cost assumptions (q8 quantization, KV cache hit expectation) to the workbook and confirm p95 numbers for 2k?

I'll follow up with a recommended contract structure (tranches + flex burst pool) and suggested billing cadence.

—Dylan
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@northforge.com>

Date: 2028-10-02T09:33:00-07:00

On Tue, Oct 2, 2028 at 09:33 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Attached: Northforge_Onramp_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal) and a sizing workbook. Karthik, can you add the perf/cost assumptions...

Arjun — quick technical notes (summary of the workbook entries):

- Workload assumptions: avg prompt+response ~900 tokens, worst-case generation 2k tokens. KV cache hit expected ~28% after warm cache for common prompts.
- Kernel/quantization: we model with q8_0 (8-bit) on A100-like instances for cost parity; for p95 target we assume asynchronous batching and 180ms per 512 token chunk at p95 on a single GPU under steady state (numbers validated on Redwood internal benchmarks with similar model family).

Sizing table (short):
- Conservative: 32 GPUs min / 48 peak. Expected p95 (2k): ~310ms. Recommended for customers with strict SLA and seasonal peaks.
- Balanced: 20 GPUs min / 36 peak. Expected p95 (2k): ~340ms. Reasonable buffer for 2–3x baseline growth over 9 months.
- Aggressive: 8 GPUs min / 24 peak (burst). Expected p95 (2k): ~420ms when bursts hit; recommend warm-start credits and a 72hr scale-up clause to move to Balanced within contract.

Ramp schedule (recommended for Balanced):
- Month 0–1: provision 12 GPUs (pilot + prewarm), activate KV cache and prefix cache for the top 200 intents.
- Month 2–3: step to 16 GPUs as concurrency grows; implement automated burst policy to move to 24 when 85% utilization sustained for 6 hours.
- Month 4–6: step to 20 GPUs; set canary rollout for model variants; enable caching optimization and model quantization to reduce nominal load.
- Month 7–9: targeted step to 28–36 GPUs depending on sustained throughput; contract triggers allow an additional tranche.

Notes on warm-up: a 48–72 hour pre-warm (synthetic replay of representative prompts) yields ~20–30% fewer cold KV misses during early weeks. We can provide a one-time warm-start credit to cover this traffic.

I'll attach the detailed perf sheet in the sizing workbook. Grace — can you add recommended SLO language and an SLA exception path when bursts exceed the committed floor?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Arjun Rao <arjun.rao@northforge.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-03T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity options — initial context

Arjun — adding the operational/SLA perspective.

- SLA: For Balanced (20 GPU floor) we can commit to 99.9% availability for the dedicated lane and p95 latency objective of <350ms for the rolling 30-day window. SLA credits apply if availability slips below that.
- Exception handling: if burst demand pushes sustained GPU utilization >90% for 12+ hrs, we'll trigger (1) automatic mitigation (prioritized queueing, temporary read-only fallbacks) and (2) a commercial trigger to move to the next tranche after a 14-day review window.
- Onboarding: recommend a 2-week pilot with 12 GPUs and a 72-hour synthetic prewarm. We'll provide runbooks and a joint runbook for incident handoffs.

We'll include the SLA language in the proposal PDF.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks team — commercial guidance from my side: for a 12-month commitment we can offer a stepped discount schedule: 10% for Balanced floor (20 GPUs), 15% for Conservative (32 GPUs), and a pilot credit for Aggressive (8 GPU) customers to cover the first-month burst usage. Add a 30-day out clause with a 60-day ramp-down fee to protect capacity planning.

Please bake the discount table into the proposal and finalize the DocuSign link. We should also include an optional flex-pool (pay-as-you-go) overlay for non-committed bursts.

Marissa
Head of Sales Ops
